angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 610,129 km at 64.57 pc = 0.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.4861 +/- 0.0127 mas (same row, RUWE 0.85): 64.57 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.877 +/- 0.008 solar radii from Bonfanti et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 108236 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...646A.157B/abstract): 610,129 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.869 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Bonfanti et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 108236 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...646A.157B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5660 +/- 61 K from Bonfanti et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 108236 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...646A.157B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonfanti et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 108236 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...646A.157B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-108236.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.491, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 108236 (pscomppars): spectral type G3 V, from Daylan et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....161...85D/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 108236 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.28 dex, from Bonfanti et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...646A.157B/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 108236 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.14997, from Bonfanti et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...646A.157B/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 108236 (pscomppars): age 6.7 Gyr, from Bonfanti et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...646A.157B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/A+A/661/A101/tableb4 (Magnetic moments of rocky planets), column Prot: 3.796 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

rotationPeriodsCatalogued.source: VizieR J/A+A/661/A101/tableb4 (Magnetic moments of rocky planets), column Prot: 3.796 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 108236 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 4.7 km/s, from Kokori et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....4K/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.877 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.402. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
